clue.text: Bomb — it is shortly about to attack

parts.note: the V1 flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: 'it is' shortened to the poetic contraction 'tis

explanation.surface: A grim warning that a bomb is moments away from striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' signals the contraction 'tis, and 'about' turns it round. 'Bomb' looks like the definition, but it gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Diseases and troubles are said to visit people, meaning to afflict or assail them.

clue.text: Old nurse finally came to me with handbook

parts.note: a VAD was a Voluntary Aid Detachment nurse of the World Wars

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of came

parts.note: taken as written
cum is Latin for with

explanation.surface: An old nurse finally arriving with a handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A vade mecum is a pocket guide carried for reference, a manual.

clue.text: Paul's companion sails off

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: The apostle's companion sets sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Acts, Silas travelled with Paul on his second missionary journey.

clue.text: One who should be just about satisfied with line of verse

definitions.text: One who should be just about satisfied
definitions.meaning: a punning description of someone who eats sparingly, a 'trim eater'
a line of three metrical feet

explanation.surface: Someone nearly content with a single line of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a cryptic definition: the answer, split as TRIM-ETER, suggests a 'trim eater', who eats lightly and so should be only just satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: A line made of three metrical feet is the meaning of the word in prosody.

clue.text: Deplore shrink that has dismissed one

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so one letter is taken out of the word for shrink

parts.note: to shrink in value is to depreciate
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A complaint about a psychiatrist who has turned a patient away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' reads as slang for a psychiatrist, but it is the verb meaning to lose value.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate is to express disapproval of something, a close synonym of deploring it.

clue.text: Where White Queen began, and ended

parts.note: in chess the queen stands on the d-file, the column named by letter d
she starts on rank one, the first row, so her opening square is d1

explanation.surface: A chess or Looking-Glass musing on where the White Queen started and finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The White Queen suggests Through the Looking-Glass, but the chess square d1 is meant: file d, rank one, read as a letter and a spelt-out number.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished and done both describe something completed.

clue.text: Special sale in food-store-that's a joke

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a pantry is a room for storing food

indicators.note: special suggests something made differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A special offer in the larder that turns out to be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' reads as part of a shop offer but signals the rearrangement; 'that's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light humorous remark, a jest.

clue.text: Avoid involving school in minor upset

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the turned word holds the abbreviation
upset means turned over, so in this down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: wee is Scots for small or minor

explanation.surface: Keeping a school out of a minor disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the Scots word round to EEW, read upwards in this down clue; 'minor upset' poses as a small disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to shun or abstain from it deliberately.

clue.text: Turning on a sixpence at first in boat

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of sixpence

parts.note: sailing is travelling in a boat

explanation.surface: A boat turning sharply in a tiny space, as on a sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning on a sixpence' is an idiom for turning in a small space; here 'Turning on' means attacking. A sixpence was a small old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on someone is to attack them suddenly, to assail them.

clue.text: Try a piece

explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is the word's old sense; a short composition is its school sense.

clue.text: American lawyer cast in a cell for time-wasting

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

indicators.note: cast here means moulded into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American lawyer thrown into a prison cell for dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges IN A CELL to LLIANCE. 'cast in a cell' pictures jail, but 'in a cell' is the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance means idle trifling or dawdling, a way of frittering away time.

clue.text: Singer's first introduction to musical performers

annotationWithheld.why: Singer's first introduction to musical performers (5) for CASTS: no parse found; 'performers' or 'musical performers' gives CAST, but S from 'Singer's first' then leaves no definition, so a word would have to do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Singer's first introduction to musical performers

clue.text: Province loses new assembly

indicators.note: loses means the province name drops a letter

parts.note: Munster is one of the four provinces of Ireland

explanation.surface: A region gives up a newly formed council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes N out of MUNSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A muster is a gathering of troops or people called together, an assembly.

clue.text: Harsh words from pro, dropped from a success

indicators.note: dropped from means one word is taken out of the following phrase

parts.note: prosperity is success, flourishing fortune
taken as written

explanation.surface: A professional sacked after a triumph, and the bitter words that followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped from' removes PRO from A PROSPERITY, leaving A SPERITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness or sharpness of tone, the quality of cutting remarks.

clue.text: Celebration of new arrival being lucky to overcome competition

indicators.note: overcome means on top of, so in this down clue the first word sits above the second

parts.note: happy can mean fortunate, as in a happy coincidence
an event is a contest in a sports programme

explanation.surface: A lucky winner celebrates a new baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A birth is the joyful occasion people celebrate when a baby arrives.

clue.text: Housemistress is to talk to girl

parts.note: to chat is to talk informally
Elaine is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boarding-school matron's job description: having a word with a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the woman in charge of a large household, its mistress.

clue.text: A trip to Saturn for him one day?

definitions.text: A trip to Saturn for him one day?

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering who might one day travel to Saturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges A and TO SATURN; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller is the person who might one day make such a voyage.

clue.text: Dishonest acts not as bad as statistics, reportedly

definitions.text: not as bad as statistics, reportedly
definitions.meaning: the saying attributed to Disraeli ranks them, then damned ones, then statistics as the worst

explanation.surface: A cynic's ranking of deceit, with statistics at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' is not a homophone signal here: it says the ranking is a famous reported saying, 'lies, damned lies and statistics'.
explanation.definitionFit: Untruths told on purpose are falsehoods, the commonest dishonest acts.

clue.text: He runs rings round hostile states -

definitions.text: He runs rings round hostile states

parts.words: He runs rings round hostile states
parts.note: he runs rings in the sense of networks of agents operating around unfriendly countries

explanation.surface: Someone who outwits enemy nations at every turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs rings round' is an idiom for outdoing; here the rings are spy networks he runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief who controls networks of secret agents is an intelligence director.

clue.text: Resolution of concern over point

indicators.note: over means on top of, so in this down clue the first word sits above the second

parts.note: a concern is a business, a firm
a ness is a headland or point

explanation.surface: Settling a worry about a detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution in the sense of determination is steadfastness.

clue.text: The best widow could offer child

definitions.meaning: in the Gospel story the poor widow gave her tiny coin, all she had
a small child is affectionately called a little one or tot

explanation.surface: A poor widow's best gift to a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'widow's mite' is the poor widow's small coin in the Gospels, praised as worth more than rich gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny coin and a tiny person share a word meaning a small thing.

clue.text: Individually wrapping wine with excellent spirit

indicators.note: wrapping means the first word is folded around the second

parts.note: singly means one at a time, individually
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Gift-wrapping bottles of wine one by one, in a generous mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excellent spirit' hints at the wine, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sportingly means behaving fairly and generously, in good spirit.

clue.text: Under plate, furtively push toast

indicators.note: under means beneath, so in this down clue the second word comes below the first

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for plate, as in a book illustration
to edge is to move or push gradually and stealthily

explanation.surface: Sneakily pushing toast under a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge someone is to drink their health, to toast them.

clue.text: Take on board a sort of blade

definitions.meaning: to accept a burden or responsibility
the scapula is known as this kind of blade

explanation.surface: Bringing some kind of blade aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept responsibility is to bear it like a load; the scapula is the bone named after that body part.

clue.text: Officer cut by fighting crowd

indicators.note: cut by means the first word is split open by the second

parts.note: SM is a sergeant major
war is fighting

explanation.surface: An officer wounded in a skirmish with a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: SM, sergeant major, is a common crossword abbreviation for a non-commissioned officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large teeming mass of people or insects.

clue.text: Spit not quite taking a game animal

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of its final letter

parts.note: to spit something is to skewer or impale it

explanation.surface: Roasting game on a spit that does not quite go through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last E from IMPALE; 'taking' adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, a game animal of the savanna.

clue.text: Clever at comprehending extremely dense page

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in, so the word at contains the rest
extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of dense

explanation.surface: Smart at understanding a very difficult page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely dense' reads as 'very difficult', but it asks for the outer letters of dense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adept means being skilled or proficient.

clue.text: Chap eating duck or grouse

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the first word contains the second

parts.note: a chap is a man
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A man dining on duck or game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts O inside MAN. 'grouse' looks like the bird, but here it means complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to grumble or complain.

clue.text: Absent Scots having way to get payment

parts.note: awa is the Scots form of away, meaning absent
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Scots who are away find a route to their wages.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum granted or paid, as in damages or a pay settlement.

clue.text: Loves running in this event

parts.note: lovers running off together to marry in secret

explanation.surface: A race in which lovers take part.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away together to wed secretly is the classic romantic escape.

clue.text: Decrepit men hate to change

indicators.note: to change these words is to reorder their letters

explanation.surface: Men who hate change growing worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges MEN, HATE and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moth-eaten is shabby and worn out, decrepit with age.

clue.text: Top player holding a single instrument

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: a star is a leading performer
one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A leading musician playing just one instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts I inside STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian lute, a stringed instrument.
